twoKindsOfOmission.description: Distinguish entity-level redaction from root keys that are never selected into the snapshot.

1_entityLevelRedaction.meaning: Keys may be present INSIDE walked roots (or entity whitelist objects) but are stripped during canonicalClone by key name. Genuine nested examples: state.world.rng and entity-level .rng fields — those sit under roots that canonicalStateSnapshot walks, so OMIT_CANONICAL_KEYS redacts them. Top-level state.rng is NOT this case (see category 2).

2_rootKeysNeverInCanonicalRootKeys.meaning: Structurally absent from the snapshot — never walked by canonicalStateSnapshot, not merely redacted. Top-level state.rng is a createGameState root field but is NOT in CANONICAL_ROOT_KEYS, so it never reaches canonicalClone and is never subject to OMIT_CANONICAL_KEYS redaction — it is simply never selected.
2_rootKeysNeverInCanonicalRootKeys.diffMethod: createGameState() root keys (src/core/gameState.js:74+) minus CANONICAL_ROOT_KEYS (sessionSamplers.js:14-19); entityList hashed via special path (see entityCoverage); state.entities Map is NOT on that path.

arrayVsMap.entityList: ordered array of live entities (gameState.js create); THIS is what canonicalStateSnapshot hashes
arrayVsMap.entities: runtime Map keyed by id for gameplay lookups (getEntity/player); NOT hashed by canonicalStateSnapshot

hashed.mechanism: canonicalStateSnapshot does NOT walk CANONICAL_ROOT_KEYS for entity data; it maps state.entityList through canonicalEntity into out.entities (sessionSamplers.js:98-101), sorted by compareEntity. The snapshot key is named 'entities' but the SOURCE is state.entityList only.
hashed.note: Do not list entityList under notableAbsentRoots: the array is hashed via this special path.

notHashed.classification: runtime lookup index keyed by id; not walked, not mapped, not folded into canonicalStateHash
notHashed.intendedRole: reconstructible runtime index derived from entityList when core spawn/sweep keep them in sync
notHashed.checkpointCaveat: A matching canonicalStateHash does NOT prove state.entities Map parity with entityList. Stale Map entries (removed entity still in Map) or missing Map entries (entity in list but not Map) share a hash yet diverge on the next getEntity/player lookup. Do not assume Map parity from a matching hash.

notableAbsentRootsNotes.rng: Top-level state.rng (mulberry32 primary stream at gameState.js create). Structurally absent from canonical snapshot — not entity-level redaction. Nested .rng keys under walked roots (e.g. state.world.rng) are category-1 redactions instead.
notableAbsentRootsNotes.entities: Top-level state.entities is a Map (id → entity) for runtime lookups. NOT hashed. Only state.entityList is hashed into snapshot field out.entities (sessionSamplers.js:98-101). Array-vs-Map: identical hash does not imply Map↔list parity; next getEntity can diverge if the index is out of sync.
notableAbsentRootsNotes.nextEntityId: gameState.js:85 entity id allocator. Absent from CANONICAL_ROOT_KEYS. Two states with identical canonicalStateHash but different nextEntityId diverge on the next spawn.
notableAbsentRootsNotes.freeIds: gameState.js:86 recycled id pool. Absent from CANONICAL_ROOT_KEYS. Same continuation-divergence class as nextEntityId.
notableAbsentRootsNotes.aiEncounter: gameState.js:124 { schemaVersion, nextSeq, commands: [] } queued AI commands. Absent from CANONICAL_ROOT_KEYS. Identical hash with different queued commands diverges when commands drain.
notableAbsentRootsNotes.npcJobs: gameState.js:144 { byId: {} } live NPC job runtime. Absent from CANONICAL_ROOT_KEYS. Divergence source for job-bearing runs with matching canonical hashes.

checkpointCriticalNotes.input: Held/edge-triggered axes and actions — two runs that differ only in input at tick N produce identical canonicalStateHash.
checkpointCriticalNotes.settings: Controls/bindings and other settings — not in CANONICAL_ROOT_KEYS; settings-differing runs hash-collide.
checkpointCriticalNotes.entities: state.entities Map is not hashed; canonicalStateHash digests entityList only (snapshot out.entities), so a matching hash does not prove Map↔entityList parity. A second entityList-derived digest cannot catch Map desync — that is already what canonicalStateHash computes. §14 needs Map inspection: direct Map↔entityList parity at checkpoint (every list entry in the Map with matching data and vice versa), deterministic Map reconstruction from entityList on restore then parity assert, or a digest over the Map's own keys/values — not over entityList
checkpointCriticalNotes.nextEntityId: Continuation-critical allocator root (gameState.js:85): not in CANONICAL_ROOT_KEYS; same hash does not guarantee next-spawn identity.
checkpointCriticalNotes.freeIds: Continuation-critical recycled-id pool (gameState.js:86): same class as nextEntityId.
checkpointCriticalNotes.aiEncounter: Continuation-critical queued AI command bag (gameState.js:124): same hash does not guarantee command-drain identity.
checkpointCriticalNotes.npcJobs: Continuation-critical live NPC job runtime (gameState.js:144): same hash does not guarantee job-runtime identity.

entropyPrimitives.continuationGap: state.rng internal counter is not part of save/observatory snapshots; only state.meta.seed is stored. Restoring a save re-seeds from meta.seed via createGameState-like paths but cannot resume mid-stream mulberry32 position from state.rng alone. Per-object drawSeeded keys can be restorable if persisted on their owners.
entropyPrimitives.continuationGapBroaderThanStateRng: The entropy continuation gap is BROADER than state.rng alone: it spans system-private mutable RNG streams inventoried under systemOwnedRngStreams. Directive §16 serializable-entropy migration must convert these unconverted paths for initial lab scenarios (Phase 1/2 concern).

systemOwnedRngStreams.auditMethod: git grep -n 'this\._rng|resetRng|_initRng|\.rng\s*=' 8610102d -- src/systems src/combat; plus mulberry32/drawSeeded/makeStream sites
systemOwnedRngStreams.conclusion: Entropy continuation gap is BROADER than state.rng. Multiple gameplay systems own private or system-local mutable RNG streams that are not part of state.rng. A checkpoint taken after such a system has consumed randomness, restored into a fresh simulation, can silently reset private streams and later diverge — unless that system uses a persisted drawSeeded rngSeed and a correct restore path.
systemOwnedRngStreams.phaseMigrationConcern: Phase 1/2: migrate system-owned streams to serializable entropy (directive §16). These are the unconverted paths for initial lab scenarios.

inputAndSettingsExclusion.fact: Because input and settings are absent from CANONICAL_ROOT_KEYS, canonicalStateHash alone is INSUFFICIENT as a checkpoint-equality oracle for input-differing or settings-differing runs. Two runs that differ only in held/edge-triggered input at tick N (or in settings) produce identical canonicalStateHash values.
inputAndSettingsExclusion.directiveSection14: Future deterministic checkpoint must add an explicit input-grammar-state digest and a settings digest; sampleAppliedInput already clones state.input for input cadence but that path is separate from canonicalStateHash.

latentContinuationCriticalRoots.fact: Same category-2 structural absence as input/settings, but for allocator/command/runtime roots: two runs with identical canonicalStateHash can still diverge on next spawn, id recycle, AI command drain, or NPC job advance.
